title: ElevenLabs go-to-market teardown
originating_prompt: how is elevenlabs promoting itself — every tactic, who runs it, and what happened when they did

run_history.prompt: how is elevenlabs promoting itself — every tactic, who runs it, and what happened when they did
re-run — add the ElevenHacks weekly series and settle the hackathon dating conflict

vocabulary: Ambassador Program — Community Builder track, Content Creator track
Affiliate Program — 22% for 12 months, run on PartnerStack
recurring_names: Thorsten Schaeff (@thorwebdev) — Head of Developer Experience, since moved to Google DeepMind
Devpost, lablab.ai, AI Tinkerers — hackathon hosting platforms
CMG Worldwide — celebrity estate rights agency
Pindrop — traced the Biden robocall to ElevenLabs
Firecrawl, Cloudflare, Replit, Cursor, Stripe — ElevenHacks weekly partners

Paid promoter programmes.description: The Ambassador Program and the affiliate programme side by side: what each pays (credits, event funding, merch; 22% of payments for 12 months via PartnerStack), who runs it, how a person joins, and whether the programme's own page asks for disclosure. One entry per programme, each linking to its page. Added for this run — the company runs two formal promoter programmes and a teardown that does not name their terms is incomplete.

Timeline of dated moves.description: Every observed promotional move in date order, one line each: the date, what happened, the URL. January 2023 to March 2026. Added for this run — it was branched to settle a dating conflict between the parent topic and Devpost, so the dates are the deliverable rather than a detail inside another section.

Paid promoter programmes.row_is: one formal programme the company runs to pay or reward people for promoting it

fields.name: programme
fields.description: The programme's own name, as the company writes it. Links to its page.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The programme's page on the company's site.

fields.name: run_by
fields.description: Team or named person operating it, and the platform it runs on where there is one (e.g. PartnerStack).

fields.name: pays
fields.description: What a participant receives, in the units the page states: cash, percentage and duration, credits, event funding, merch. Not a summary — the terms.

fields.name: how_to_join
fields.description: Application, invitation, or open signup, and any stated bar.

fields.name: disclosure_required
fields.description: required | encouraged | silent — what the programme's own page asks of participants. `silent` means the page says nothing, which is itself the finding.

fields.name: first_seen
fields.description: YYYY-MM-DD the programme was first observed running.

Paid promoter programmes.render: One row per programme. The programme name is the link. A cell with nothing behind it is `—`, never a guess.

Timeline of dated moves.row_is: one observed promotional move on one date

fields.name: date
fields.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Where sources disagree, the date the primary source gives, with the conflict noted in `dispute`.

fields.name: move
fields.description: What happened, one line, in the vocabulary the company uses for it.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Where the move can be seen. A move with no reachable URL is recorded in audit.md as a known-gap, not dropped.

fields.name: channel
fields.description: Where it happened — the source or platform.

fields.name: dispute
fields.description: Empty unless sources disagree on the date; then both readings and who says which.

Timeline of dated moves.render: One line per row: date — move ([link](url)). Rows carrying a `dispute` show both dates.

angles.label: dated-channel-appearances
angles.query: ElevenLabs Summit November 2025, SXSW premiere March 2026, Oracle Park sponsorship, Product Hunt GenFM, Devpost and lablab.ai listings — one occurrence per date with a URL
angles.rationale: The teardown needs a worked example per occurrence, not a channel list.

angles.label: repeatable-programme-tactics
angles.query: ElevenHacks weekly hackathons, Worldwide Hackathon with a16z, Startup Grants, Iconic Voices estate deals — when each started, how often it repeated, what changed each time
angles.rationale: A tactic run once is an anecdote; a tactic run eleven times is the motion. Sources disagree on when the 33-city hackathon ran — the parent topic says December 2025, Devpost says February — so settling the dates is part of this angle.

angles.label: promoter-handles-and-disclosure
angles.query: posts by @matistanis, @LukeHarries_, @thorwebdev, u/J-ElevenLabs; Ambassador Program tracks; affiliate links paying 22% — dated examples with and without disclosure
angles.rationale: Feeds promoter_network.csv, this command's own output. The contested part is whether paying creators in credits rather than cash counts as disclosed sponsorship, so collect what each promoter wrote alongside what they were paid in.

angles.label: backlash-and-repercussions
angles.query: 4chan voice abuse January 2023, Biden robocall traced by Pindrop, Illinois BIPA class actions, r/ElevenLabs moderator removals, Hacker News astroturfing accusations
angles.rationale: What happened when they promoted is half the question — including the argument running underneath it, whether consent from an estate is consent at all.

angles.label: observed-reach-per-tactic
angles.query: hackathon applicant and submission counts, grants awarded, ElevenHacks prize pool, launch video view counts, Product Hunt upvotes, Hacker News points
angles.rationale: Reach numbers separate a tactic that worked from one that was merely run.

sources_unavailable.reason: the user handed over no documents
